## Model card

# Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct

Qwen2.5 is the latest series of Qwen large language models. This repo contains the instruction-tuned 0.5B model.

## Quickstart

Use it through any OpenAI-compatible client: send chat messages, get a reply.

## Evaluation

Detailed results are in the Qwen2.5 blog.

## Architecture

From `config.json`:

| field | value | what it means |
|---|---|---|
| `model_type` | qwen2 | The family name transformers uses to pick the model code. |
| `architectures` | Qwen2ForCausalLM | The class name that loads these weights; MAX matches on this. |
| `hidden_size` | 896 | Width of the residual stream: the size of every token's vector as it moves through the layers. |
| `num_hidden_layers` | 24 | How many transformer blocks are stacked. Depth. |
| `num_attention_heads` | 14 | Query heads per layer; each looks at the context in its own learned way. |
| `num_key_value_heads` | 2 | Key/value heads. Fewer than query heads means grouped-query attention (GQA): query heads share K/V, which shrinks the KV cache. |
| `gqa_ratio` | 7:1 | Query heads per KV head. Higher means a smaller KV cache for the same context. |
| `head_dim` | 64 | Size of each attention head. |
| `intermediate_size` | 4864 | Hidden width of the MLP (feed-forward) block, usually 3-4x hidden_size. |
| `vocab_size` | 151936 | Number of tokens the model knows; sets the embedding and output matrix size. |
| `max_position_embeddings` | 32768 | Longest context the model was trained to handle. |
| `rope_theta` | 1000000.0 | RoPE base frequency; larger values stretch positional encoding for longer contexts. |
| `tie_word_embeddings` | True | True means the output matrix reuses the input embeddings, saving vocab x hidden parameters. |

## Try it

These cells talk to your local `mxc` endpoint. Opened from the console's Notebook panel, they just work. Started yourself (`mxc learn`, `jupyter lab`), set `MXC_API_KEY` (and optionally `MXC_BASE_URL`) in the environment before starting Jupyter.

import os
BASE_URL = (os.environ.get("MXC_BASE_URL") or os.environ.get("HOTFIRE_BASE_URL")
            or os.environ.get("MST_BASE_URL") or "http://127.0.0.1:11435/v1")
API_KEY = (os.environ.get("MXC_API_KEY") or os.environ.get("HOTFIRE_API_KEY") or os.environ["MST_API_KEY"])  # create one with: mxc keys new <app>
MODEL = "qwen2.5-0.5b"
print(BASE_URL, MODEL)

from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI(base_url=BASE_URL, api_key=API_KEY)
reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model=MODEL,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "In one sentence, what are you?"}],
)
print(reply.choices[0].message.content)

import httpx
r = httpx.post(
    f"{BASE_URL}/chat/completions",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}"},
    json={"model": MODEL, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hi."}]},
    timeout=120,
)
r.raise_for_status()
print(r.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"])
